derive-packet-unicode-16-digit-title.reason: Adopt for #195, porting bench/tools/derive_packet.py to the Rust derive-packet, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-18. Changes behavior on purpose: derive_packet.py matched the H1 issue number with \d, so the digits it accepted depended on the interpreter's Unicode database; Python 3.12, which CI uses, has Unicode 15.0. The Rust title check is fixed at the Unicode 16.0 decimal digits (category Nd) that Python 3.14 matches, for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: a title changes when it is numbered with a Unicode 16.0 decimal digit that the former interpreter's Unicode database lacks. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is the 80 digits added in Unicode 16.0 (U+10D40..U+10D49, U+116D0..U+116E3, U+11BF0..U+11BF9, U+16130..U+16139, U+16D70..U+16D79, U+1CCF0..U+1CCF9, U+1E5F1..U+1E5FA). Older interpreters lack more: Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) lacks 110, those 80 and 30 added in Unicode 14.0 and 15.0 (U+11F50..U+11F59, U+16AC0..U+16AC9, U+1E4F0..U+1E4F9). None of the repository's tracked files contains any of the 110. This case pins acceptance: on Python 3.13 or older (Unicode 15.1 or earlier), derive_packet.py refused this title with 'H1 title: expected exactly one, found 0'; Rust accepts it, as Python 3.14 does.

derive-packet-unassigned-path.reason: Adopt for #206, part of #154, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py. Changes behavior on purpose, toward Python: the Rust repr escaped only assigned non-printable characters and noncharacters, so it wrote unassigned code points such as U+0378 as-is, while every Python version escapes them; derive_packet.py on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14 quotes this name as 'missing-\u0378.md'. The Rust repr escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), checked against Python 3.14 for every code point, for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. The same pytext::repr quotes input in every bench-tools command's diagnostics. Compatibility impact: none against any Python interpreter for code points unassigned in Unicode 16.0; Rust output before this change differed for every such code point.

derive-packet-unicode-15-1-path.reason: Adopt for #206, part of #154, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. derive_packet.py's repr followed the running interpreter's Unicode database, so it escaped characters that database lacked. The Rust repr escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), checked against Python 3.14 for every code point, for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. The same pytext::repr quotes input in every bench-tools command's diagnostics. Compatibility impact: a quoted name changes when it holds a character assigned after the former interpreter's Unicode version. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0, which 3.12 escapes and Rust writes as-is; none the other way. Older interpreters differ on more: Python 3.13 (Unicode 15.1) on 5,185, the Unicode 16.0 additions, and Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) on 11,130. This case pins U+2EBF0, added in Unicode 15.1: derive_packet.py on Python 3.12 or older quoted the name as 'missing-\U0002ebf0.md'; Rust writes the character, as Python 3.13 and 3.14 do.

derive-packet-dot-digit-out.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name derive_packet.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: a value made of a dash, digits and dots, such as -.5, was read as a value, as argparse reads a negative number. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads a dash-led argument as a value only when it parses as a number with a digit before any dot, so -.5 is an unexpected argument, exit 2; -5 and -1.5 remain values. Rationale: allow_negative_numbers has no setting for argparse's rule, and emulating argparse would keep the hand-written parsing #215 removes; no caller passes such a value. Compatibility impact: give the value attached, as --out=-.5, which still works; the deleted bench/tools/derive_packet.py wrote the packet to -.5 under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.

derive-packet-exponent-out.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name derive_packet.py. Changes accepted input on purpose, toward Python 3.14. Old behavior: a dash-led value holding a letter, such as -1e5, was refused as an option, exit 2, as Python 3.12's argparse refuses it. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads -1e5 as a negative number in exponent form and takes it as the value, as Python 3.14's argparse does, which takes any argument that starts with a dash and a digit. Rationale: clap's allow_negative_numbers rule; keeping 3.12's refusal would need hand-written parsing #215 removes. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs, and no caller passes such a value; the deleted bench/tools/derive_packet.py refused -1e5 under Python 3.12 and took it under 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.

derive-packet-help-with-attached-argumen.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name derive_packet.py. Changes behavior on purpose, toward Python. Old behavior: bench-tools derive-packet refused -hx, an argument attached to -h, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap reads -hx as -h then -x and prints help, exit 0, as argparse does under Python 3.12 and 3.14; build-packet already printed help. Rationale: clap's short-option rule. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now prints help and runs nothing; the deleted bench/tools/derive_packet.py printed help too under Python 3.12 and 3.14. Resolving issue: #215.
